proof:
Source: step 6 of the parent's supplied proof, with the profile φ reduced to the two properties that step uses (φ is C^infinity, and φ = 1 on (−∞, 1/2]). In Lean, ContDiff ℝ (⊤ : ℕ∞) means C^infinity.

1. By contDiff_iff_contDiffAt, ζ is C^infinity iff it is C^infinity at every point. Fix x ∈ R^m. We show ζ is C^infinity at x in two cases: x = ξ and x ≠ ξ.

2. Case x = ξ.
  - Since ρ/2 > 0, the open ball B°(ξ, ρ/2) = {y : ‖y − ξ‖ < ρ/2} is a neighbourhood of ξ (Metric.ball_mem_nhds).
  - For y in this ball, dist(y, ξ) = ‖y − ξ‖ < ρ/2. Since ρ > 0, this gives ‖y − ξ‖/ρ < 1/2, in particular <= 1/2. The hypothesis on φ then gives ζ(y) = φ(‖y − ξ‖/ρ) = 1.
  - So ζ agrees with the constant function 1 on a neighbourhood of ξ.
  - Constant functions are C^infinity (contDiffAt_const), and being C^infinity at a point depends only on the germ (ContDiffAt.congr_of_eventuallyEq). Hence ζ is C^infinity at ξ.

3. Case x ≠ ξ.
  - Then x − ξ ≠ 0, and y ↦ y − ξ is C^infinity (identity minus a constant).
  - The Euclidean norm of the inner product space R^m is C^infinity at every nonzero point (contDiffAt_norm), in particular at x − ξ. By the chain rule (ContDiffAt.comp), y ↦ ‖y − ξ‖ is C^infinity at x.
  - Dividing by the constant ρ keeps this (ContDiffAt.div_const), so y ↦ ‖y − ξ‖/ρ is C^infinity at x.
  - φ is C^infinity on R, so it is C^infinity at ‖x − ξ‖/ρ (ContDiff.contDiffAt). The chain rule again shows that ζ = φ ∘ (y ↦ ‖y − ξ‖/ρ) is C^infinity at x.

4. Every x falls in case 2 or case 3. So ζ is C^infinity at every point, hence C^infinity on R^m by step 1. ∎
key_steps: Reduce to C^∞ at every point (contDiff_iff_contDiffAt)
At x = ξ: ζ ≡ 1 on the open ball B°(ξ, ρ/2), a neighbourhood of ξ, so ζ is C^∞ at ξ (contDiffAt_const.congr_of_eventuallyEq)
At x ≠ ξ: y ↦ ‖y − ξ‖/ρ is C^∞ at x (contDiffAt_norm at x − ξ ≠ 0, chain rule, div_const), and composing with the C^∞ map φ gives C^∞ at x
